lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Concept model B: variability and overlap

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Compare these two examples. Find the step where they stop being the same.

items.prompt: A data set is: 17, 25, 16, 22, with a mean of 20. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of this data set?

steps: Find each value's distance from the mean: |17-20| = 3, |25-20| = 5, |16-20| = 4, |22-20| = 2.
Divide by the number of values: 14 ÷ 4 = 3 1/2.

items.prompt: Two data sets have means of 30 and 42. Their mean absolute deviation (MAD) is 4. Express the difference between the means as a multiple of the MAD.

steps: Find the difference between the means: 42 − 30 = 12.
The means differ by 3 times the MAD.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Sample A: 33, 42, 50, 47, 28. Sample B: 60, 55, 59, 56, 20. Based on the means, which sample tends to have greater values?
choices: Sample A, with a mean of 40 compared to 50.
Sample B, with a mean of 50 compared to 40.
Sample B, with a mean of 40 compared to 50.
Both samples have the same mean.

items.prompt: Sample A: 27, 20, 27, 24, 16. Sample B: 22, 20, 23, 17, 23. Based on the range of each sample, which sample is more consistent (less variable)?
choices: Sample B, with a range of 11 compared to 6.
Sample B, with a range of 6 compared to 11.
Sample A, with a range of 11 compared to 6.
Both samples have the same range.

items.prompt: A researcher wants to know about all 272 commuters on a train line. She randomly selects 66 of them to survey. What is the sample in this situation?
choices: The researcher's own estimate
The 66 randomly selected commuters on a train line
Only the first 66 commuters on a train line on a list
All 272 commuters on a train line

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A student picks a random starting point, then surveys every 10th person from the full numbered list of students at Lincoln Middle School, for a total of 17. Is this sampling method likely to produce a representative sample?
choices: No, likely not representative, because the population is too large.
Yes, likely representative — every member had a fair, known chance of being chosen.
No, likely not representative — the method favors certain members over others.
Yes, likely representative, because the sample size is large enough.

items.prompt: In a random sample of 22 commuters on a train line, 19 preferred a new park design. Based on this sample, about how many of the 110 commuters on a train line would you expect to prefer a new park design?
Five random samples of the same population produced these mean scores: 20, 13, 20, 20, 12. What is the range of these sample estimates?

A population has 4770 students at Lincoln Middle School. Student A takes a random sample of 8. Student B takes a random sample of 44. Both use proper random selection. Whose sample is more likely to give an estimate closer to the true population value?
choices: Student B's sample of 44, because larger random samples tend to produce more consistent, accurate estimates.
Student A's sample of 8, because smaller samples are easier to analyze.
Neither sample is reliable unless it includes the entire population.
Both are equally likely to be accurate, because both are random.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: A student surveys 57 students at Lincoln Middle School using a simple random sample and records the results. Is it valid to generalize this result to all 1596 students at Lincoln Middle School?
choices: No, because samples can never be generalized to a population.
Yes, because the sample was selected randomly, so it is likely representative of the population.
Yes, because the sample size is large enough regardless of how it was chosen.
No, because the sample was not randomly selected, so it may not represent the population.

items.prompt: A sample of 7 values is: 26, 33, 20, 40, 54, 51, 26. What is the median of this data set?
